prompt: our new hire wrote tests for the config package and something feels off about them, can you review and fix? dont break anything, the suite is green
assertions: Per-symbol tests are consolidated into whole-package contract scenarios and/or runnable examples (package-level Example() or a TestConfig-style scenario both welcome)
TestDebugDump deleted; the sleep-based concurrent smoke DELETED with the docs-promise-no-concurrency reasoning; the internals-reaching assertion goes through the exported surface
The benchmark uses b.Loop and meaningfully exercises Load
The review flags Load's string-only errors and recommends or introduces typed/sentinel errors (errors.Is/As or Go 1.26 errors.AsType); graded from code AND report.md
Malformed-input cases are named (not dumped as multiline strings into logs), reusing existing fixture fields where possible rather than inventing new ones
At least one runnable example exists and follows the audience rules; sample-config comments carry real information (demonstrate the syntax, explain a field's role), never filler

Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)

Runnable examples speak to pkgsite users about the attributed symbol/scenario: the doc comment never narrates the code or addresses maintainers, and in-function comments explain non-obvious inputs and contract behavior at the call sites
STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... zero failures and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes
report.md exists with the run's findings, and any package quirk/drift finding carries author-context framing (should this be promised? would that harden the contract?) rather than a bare observation
